repo.description:
### Impact
A vulnerability chain in Jellyfin has been discovered which potentially allows a non-admin user with SubtitleManagement permission to achieve remote code execution as root.

The subtitle upload endpoint (`POST /Videos/{itemId}/Subtitles`) does not validate the Format field, allowing path traversal via the file extension. This enables arbitrary file write, which chains into potential arbitrary file read (via `.strm` files), database extraction, admin privilege escalation, and ultimately RCE via ld.so.preload.

This vulnerability requires an administrator or a user to have been explicitly granted the "Upload Subtitles" permission.

### Patches
This issue has been fixed in 10.11.7 (and backported to `master`) via improved sanitization of the affected API endpoint.

### Workarounds
Do not grant non-administrator users Subtitle upload permissions to reduce attack surface.

### References

Proof of concept provided by @odgrso via private report document.
Proof-of-concept provided by @LTe to be released alongside this GHSA: https://github.com/LTe/jellyfin-subtitiles-exploit

This bug was also reported in parallel by GHSL team member [@anticomputer (Bas)](https://github.com/anticomputer) though without the exploit chaining (GHSL-2026-051).
repo.summary: Potential RCE via subtitle upload path traversal + .strm chain
